editorial.headline: Wireless Networks: Open Nationally and Outside Bali’s PMA Moratorium
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers terrestrial wireless network infrastructure and capacity, open to foreign investment nationally and not blocked by Bali’s risk-based PMA moratorium at large scale.
editorial.body:
Wireless Telecommunications Activities concerns the infrastructure behind wireless communication on the earth’s surface: operating, maintaining, or providing networks that use electromagnetic waves to transmit voice, data, text, audio, and video. It is an activity defined by the network itself, rather than by a single kind of message or customer. The work may involve the technical backbone through which communications travel wirelessly, from the infrastructure’s operation to its continuing upkeep.

Its scope spans infrastructure for both fixed and mobile services. Fixed networks may include fixed broadband, wireless broadband access, or microwave-link communication systems; mobile networks may include cellular service or radio-based systems such as radio trunking. It also includes leasing wireless network capacity to other telecommunications-network operators or telecommunications-service operators. In practical terms, this is an activity for businesses providing and running the wireless network layer, including the capacity on which other operators may rely.

The activity is open across the listed business scales: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. Nationally, its PMA status is TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. That makes the national position unusually direct: foreign investment is open up to the stated ceiling, while the activity remains available at every listed scale. The relevant national reference is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021.

Bali requires a more careful reading, but not a more pessimistic one. The province permanently blocks PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk activities across the island. This activity is not blocked by that moratorium. At the Besar scale, its OSS risk is stated as Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, which places it beyond the risk bands covered by the provincial prohibition. For an activity operating at large scale in Bali, the stated risk level puts it outside that moratorium’s blocked bands. The Bali position is therefore OK_or_HIGHER_RISK: open in the sense that the moratorium does not block it, while its large-scale risk classification remains central to the local picture.
